topic: BPMN process model driven multi-agent workflow automation
scale: 0 = not satisfied, 0.5 = partially satisfied, 1 = satisfied; null = not yet scored

entries.title: BPMN-Based Design of Multi-Agent Systems: Personalized Language Learning Workflow Automation with RAG-Enhanced Knowledge Access
entries.notes: Scaffold marks is_preprint=false, but the PDF header reads 'Not peer-reviewed version' (Preprints.org 10.20944), so peer_reviewed_venue scored 0; grey-literature items are not present in this record's checklist and were not added. BPMN compiled 1:1 into LangGraph nodes is a clear aim, and RAGAs/WER/pilot-survey metrics are defined, but the extraction records no baseline: hallucination reduction 'compared to a baseline single-agent LLM' is asserted with the figures explicitly '(not shown)', so no comparison was demonstrated. MDPI Data Availability Statement is the unfilled boilerplate template; nothing released. Limitations (proprietary GPT-4/Whisper, teacher-in-the-loop bottleneck, Luxembourgish only, n=14 short-term pilot) are stated but there is no threats-to-validity analysis.

entries.title: Accountable Multi-Agent AI Systems: Orchestration Frameworks for Enterprise Workflow Automation with Human-in-the-Loop Verification
entries.notes: Single-author Zenodo deposit (Prateek Dutta, 'AI Fullstack Developer & Independent Researcher') with no peer review. The design in principle has the right shape - control is the same LLM and tool configuration with HITL gates disabled - and numbers are reported (94.7% mean UAAR reduction, throughput at 87.3% of baseline), so baseline_or_control is partial rather than absent. But three enterprise deployments are unnamed, no model is identified, no per-deployment sample sizes, no statistical test, and no artefacts; UAAR is never operationalised. A full-text search finds no limitations or threats-to-validity section at all. Uniformly high, precise figures (96.2 / 93.4 / 94.5) across three unnamed sites with zero verifiable detail do not support the conclusions drawn.

entries.title: A Privacy-Preserving On-Device Multi-Agent Architecture for AI PC (POMA) Workflow Automation
entries.notes: Intel Corporation, IEEE ICAD 2026. Aims and the RQ1 metric pair are stated unusually cleanly (task completion rate and policy overhead alongside attack success rate, unsafe action rate, true block rate, escalation accuracy, confirmation burden), which earns full marks on metrics_defined. Section VII is a proposed evaluation methodology: the three baselines (CUA without verifier gating, single-agent end-to-end, cloud-first) and the Policy Verifier / provenance / escalation ablations are planned, not executed, and no results are reported, so baseline_or_control is 0. Credit on conclusions_supported because the paper claims only design properties and does not present unrun evaluation as evidence. No limitations section; open weaknesses appear only as future work.

entries.title: GALENA: A Governance-Aware LLM Enterprise Navigation Architecture for Autonomous Multi-Agent Workflow Automation with Compliance Enforcement
entries.notes: Single-author paper (Narasimha Rao Boinapalli) in Excel International Journal of Technology, Engineering and Management under a self-minted DOI prefix (10.64971), so peer_reviewed_venue is partial at best. Six baselines with reported numbers (TCA 0.97 vs 0.82; GVR 0.03 vs 0.11) give a nominal comparison, but the 4,800-task workload is in-house, nothing is released, the configuration names a model version that could not be corroborated, and every one of five metrics against every baseline is reported at p < 0.001 - implausibly uniform. metrics_defined is partial because the governance violation rate is measured by the same governance engine under test, which is circular. A Limitations section exists but covers system overheads (23 ms, 3-5% classifier FP, manual constraint set), not study validity. Conclusions are not supportable from the evidence presented.

entries.title: A stigmergy-driven multi-agent framework for intelligent task orchestration
entries.notes: Master's thesis (Eva Veli, URV/UB/UPC) - examined, not peer-reviewed, hence 0 on venue. Strongest evaluation design in the corpus: 790 controlled runs over nine ablation configurations, an explicit coordination-free baseline (C7) plus round-robin, a 2x2 factorial analysis of the two validation layers, temperature 0, and Cliff's delta reported because the N=5 paired Wilcoxon tests are underpowered - the authors say so themselves. Full prototype released at github.com/evaveli/agentcy. Threats are handled thoroughly (residual non-determinism, single synthetic domain, single model, single-rater survey coding with no IRR). Garousi: authority 0.5 as a student thesis with a named supervisor but no track record; objectivity 1 for reporting the dissociation that accuracy stayed at 0.98 while violation detection fell to 0%; novelty_impact 0.5 given the synthetic domain and unpublished status.

entries.title: Open-Rosalind: Tool-First Biomedical LLM Agents with Process-Aware Benchmarking
entries.notes: arXiv-class preprint (Liang Wang, Huazhong University of Science and Technology). 1,770 runs across six model families with paired seed replications, cluster-aware permutation tests, a free-form ReAct baseline plus four separately ablated constraints (no_tool, no_cite, no_template), and an author-independent hold-out. System, benchmark, hold-out data and per-task traces released MIT at github.com/maris205/open-rosalind. conclusions_supported is 1 precisely because the paper publishes results that cut against its own framing: removing the template barely moved accuracy (81.4 -> 80.5), and the constrained pipeline collapsed to 17.8% on the independent hold-out, below both ReAct and no_tool. Garousi authority 0.5 - single author, institutional affiliation but no visible track record; objectivity 1 for the diagnosis-and-repair reporting.

entries.title: Context is key for cybersecurity: leveraging external knowledge for process model explanation via LLMs
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed Springer journal (International Journal of Information Security, 3 authors, University of Regensburg). Two real-world cases (93 ISO 27001 questions, 71 IEC 62443 questions), an explicit 'nothing' control giving parametric-knowledge-only performance, five prompting strategies, manual grading plus an LLM judge validated against humans with Cohen's kappa. Limitations are extensive and specific. Data Availability states 'No datasets were generated or analysed'; the question catalogues are not released, so artefacts score 0. conclusions_supported reduced to 0.5 for an internal inconsistency: input-interpretation failures are reported as 12 in the error typology and as 4 in the discussion.

entries.title: E2E Process Automation Leveraging Generative AI and IDP-Based Automation Agent: A Case Study on Corporate Expense Processing
entries.notes: Samsung SDS industrial deployment report (5 authors, Bon View journal, peer-reviewed). Design is a one-month single-site pilot with no comparison arm, so baseline_or_control is 0. The confusion matrix over 1,448 receipts is properly defined (TP 1,073, TN 133, FP 0, FN 242 -> accuracy 0.83, precision 1.00, recall 0.82, F1 0.90). conclusions_supported is partial: the headline 80-90% monthly saving is explicitly presented under 'expected quantitative effects based on general intelligent automation adoption cases' rather than measured, which the authors are honest about but which does not evidence the E2E automation claim. Limitations are about deployment cost, explainability and change management rather than study validity; no artefacts (proprietary receipt data).

entries.title: CAPRI: A Context-Aware Privacy Framework for Multi-Agent Generative AI Applications
entries.notes: IEEE Access (Georgia Tech; second author an IEEE Fellow). A real control condition exists - an out-of-the-box ToolEmu ReAct prompt on unmodified tool definitions - and four configurations are compared with numbers, so baseline_or_control is 1. Design is only partial: 50 questions total across two ToolEmu toolsets, no repetitions, no statistical test, and the local gatekeeper is a 4-bit quantized Llama 3.1 8B chosen for GPU constraints. Metrics (success rate, conversational turns) are clearly defined but the paper reports no privacy-violation metric at all despite the privacy framing, which is why conclusions_supported is 0.5. Limitations amount to a remark that GPT-3.5 Turbo capped success at 64%. No artefacts.

entries.title: Retail Resilience Engine: An Agentic AI Framework for Building Reliable Retail Systems With Test-Driven Development Approach
entries.notes: IEEE Access, but the reported numbers contradict themselves across sections: the abstract and conclusion claim a 97.5% similarity index while the body reports a Pearson correlation of 0.96, and prompt-filtering accuracy is given as 98.2%, 98.20% and 98.22% in different places. That is a validity problem, so conclusions_supported is 0 and metrics_defined is 0.5. The comparator is human experts rather than another agent configuration, and the alignment experiment rests on ten queries with ten domains for robustness, so design and baseline are partial. There is a genuine Section V limitations discussion (privacy, black-box operation, heuristic hyperparameters, cloud-only design), which is credited. Nothing released.

entries.title: Solver-Aided Verification of Policy Compliance in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
entries.notes: Preprint from University of Washington (René Just's group). This is a direct RQ1 contrast: the same airline policy supplied as a natural-language document in context versus compiled SMT-LIB constraints checked by Z3 as a pre-condition on every planned tool call, on tau2-bench with 50 tasks x 4 trials and pass^k reporting. Both dependent variables are reported together (invalid write calls down to 29%; pass^1 0.560 -> 0.625). Threats are handled well, including a rare negative result - four successive designs for compiling policy into logic failed on syntactic correctness, semantic completeness or constraint tightness until manual review was added, so the gain is contingent on human-curated encodings. No artefact release found, hence 0 there. Garousi items all strong.

entries.title: Compliance Digital Twins for Autonomous Financial Agents: Reliability-Aware Scenario Assurance via Calibrated LLM Evaluation
entries.notes: Single author (Wells Fargo) in the Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research - a crisis-communication journal publishing a financial-agent systems paper, so peer_reviewed_venue is 0.5 at most. The decisive design problem is a construct mismatch: agent behaviour is a probabilistic but scripted decision model, not an LLM agent, so the detection gains measure the assurance harness rather than agent behaviour under process constraints. Numbers also contradict: the baseline detection rate is 43% in the text and 71/150 = 47% in the per-family table, making the headline '46 percentage-point improvement' inconsistent with the paper's own table (89 - 47 = 42). threats_discussed scores 1 for an unusually candid Section 5.2.7 that concedes the scripted agents and the single synthetic workflow and calls the results indicative rather than definitive.

entries.title: Near-Miss: Latent Policy Failure Detection in Agentic Workflows
entries.notes: IBM Research preprint. 50 tau2-verified Airlines tasks x 4 trials x 6 agents (200 simulations per agent), with the conventional final-state reference evaluation as the explicit comparator and the detector validated against human annotation (generated-code search reached precision 1.00 / recall 1.00). Code released at github.com/AgentToolkit/toolguard-violation-analysis. Limitations are candid: bounded by ToolGuard guard-code quality, offline evaluation only, single benchmark, and annotation by the authors rather than independent annotators. The paper also flags its own Qwen2.5-72b measurement as unreliable rather than reporting it straight. Peer-review status is the only gap.

entries.title: From Business Events to Auditable Decisions: Ontology-Governed Graph Simulation for Enterprise AI
entries.notes: Vendor preprint (Yonyou AI Lab / Yonyou Network Technology, 8 authors). The headline comparison is confounded and the authors concede it: LOM-action is fine-tuned while the Doubao-1.8 and DeepSeek-V3.2 baselines are zero-shot, and the controlled ablation that would isolate the architecture from the training (same fine-tuning without the Phase 2 simulation curriculum) has not been run. That caps design_appropriate, baseline_or_control and conclusions_supported at 0.5 even though numbers are reported for every task. All experiments use synthetic Neo4j subgraphs of 20-30 nodes, far below enterprise scale. The illusive-accuracy index (answer accuracy minus tool-chain F1) is a well-defined and genuinely useful metric. Garousi objectivity 0.5 for the vendor interest, offset by the conceded confound; no artefacts released.

entries.title: Provably Secure Agent Guardrail
entries.notes: USTC preprint with an established security group (Weiming Zhang, Kejiang Chen, Nenghai Yu). Head-to-head against the two mechanisms practitioners actually deploy - stateless ABAC and LLM-as-a-Judge - across six front-end models, with accuracy, false-alarm rate, F1 and latency reported. Archived code at github.com/Dizzy-K/ePCA. design_appropriate is 0.5 because both environments are constructed micro-benchmarks and the authors themselves call the experiments illustrative realizations rather than statistically representative benchmarks. conclusions_supported is 0.5: the title claims provable security while the paper correctly concedes that the verifier proves absence of violations of explicitly defined axioms, not absence of unsafe behaviour - an honest bound that the framing overstates.

entries.title: SARC: A Governance-by-Architecture Framework for Agentic AI Systems
entries.notes: Single-author arXiv preprint (Gaston Besanson, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella) - but unlike the other single-author records here it releases code and reproducibility artefacts at github.com/besanson/sarc-governance, runs 50 seeds x 1,000 orders across five governance regimes with 95% CIs and a predicate-noise sweep, and states three explicit threats to validity. design_appropriate is 0.5 because the agent is a simulated procurement policy rather than an LLM, and the authors state that per-step latency figures are model parameters of each regime rather than measurements. conclusions_supported earns 1 for unusually careful attribution: the 89.5% reduction in soft-window overages is credited to the declared throttling response placed at the post-action auditor, with the authors noting a policy-as-code system with the same response would perform similarly.

entries.title: ProAgent: From Robotic Process Automation to Agentic Process Automation
entries.notes: Preprint from Tsinghua / MIT / CMU / ModelBest / Renmin (12 authors), code public at github.com/OpenBMB/ProAgent. Evidence is a single GPT-4 proof of concept on n8n: one commercial worksheet-routing task, a seven-node constructed workflow and two illustrated executions. No metrics, no baseline, no compliance measurement, so those items are 0. conclusions_supported is 0.5 because paradigm-level claims about Agentic Process Automation rest on that single example. Garousi authority 1 for the group's track record and novelty_impact 1 for the APA framing and the AWDL DataAgent/ControlAgent vocabulary, but methodology and objectivity are 0.5 - it is advocacy for a proposed paradigm, tempered by a genuine safety discussion of automation bias and hallucination.

entries.title: Towards Enforcing Company Policy Adherence in Agentic Workflows
entries.notes: The strongest record in the corpus and the closest peer-reviewed test of RQ1: EMNLP 2025 Industry Track (ACL), IBM Research, 6 authors. Agent, tools and task are held fixed while natural-language policy in the prompt is swapped for compiled deterministic ToolGuard pre-conditions, and two reflection controls isolate the effect of merely restating the policy (pass^10 0.227 baseline, 0.273 for both reflection variants, 0.500 with guards). Because tau-bench scores final database state against the annotated goal state, compliance and task completion are measured together rather than traded off. Code and data at github.com/IBM/tool_guard. Limitations are stated precisely - pre-tool-activation only, so violations of omission are not caught, and a single benchmark with concise policies.

entries.title: Policy-Invisible Violations in LLM-Based Agents
entries.notes: Atlassian preprint (2 authors). Three-way comparison on identical traces - no enforcement, the same policy injected as natural-language rules in the system prompt, and world-state grounded enforcement - which is exactly the RQ1 contrast; all 600 baseline and 600 policy-in-prompt traces were human-reviewed. Separate Threats to Validity (6.4) and Limitations (6.5) sections name the single curated domain, 120 cases at 7-8 per category, an execution-oriented system prompt that likely inflates violation rates, single-run measurement and a small annotator pool. Objectivity is high despite Sentinel being their own system: they report its 5 false positives, 37 missed violations, and recall falling monotonically to 20% as world-model coverage degrades. No artefact release found.

entries.title: MANTRA: Synthesizing SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using LLM Agents
entries.notes: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems preprint (4 authors). 285 SMT-cross-validated cases across six domains with forward and backward Z3 conflict searches; code at anonymous.4open.science and benchmark data on HuggingFace. baseline_or_control is 0.5 rather than 1 because the agent results are a six-model cross-comparison plus a feature-level comparison against other benchmarks, not an intervention-versus-control condition - the process model functions as an oracle while every agent receives the same natural-language manual. Limitations are extensive and self-critical: no formal certification of compliance with the original document, a fixed horizon h=16, unresolved scenarios needing human review, and benchmark generation that is not fully reproducible because it uses a proprietary LLM agent.

entries.title: Evaluation of Automated Machinery Functional Safety Risk Assessment Using LLMs
entries.notes: IEEE Access (innotec GmbH + University of Applied Sciences Osnabrück). The cleanest controlled ablation of the RQ1 contrast in the corpus, even though it is single-turn classification rather than an agent: the explicit ISO 13849-1 Annex A risk graph injected as deterministic S/F/P rules versus a zero-shot prompt carrying only the hazard description, over 7,800 scenarios with stratified subsets, temperature 0, three repeated runs in Test 2 and a cross-architecture Test 3. Zero-shot 0.300-0.470 rises to 0.990-1.000 with rules. Threats are handled properly (templated descriptions inducing recognition bias, PLr accuracy as only a proxy for expert safety reasoning, proprietary version drift). data_or_artifacts_available is 0.5: the underlying standards-aligned dataset is cited as publicly available but no code or prompt repository is released.

entries.title: Comparing Generative Chatbots Based on Process Requirements: A Case Study
entries.notes: IEEE BigData 2023, University of Waterloo (5 authors). Tests the weakest form of the intervention - BPMN XML supplied as prompt context with no engine enforcing it - across 13 evaluation questions on a single Trip Planning model, scored qualitatively by the authors. The GPT-3.5 versus PaLM 2 comparison is a model comparison, not a natural-language-instruction control, and there is no process-engine-enforced condition, so baseline_or_control is 0.5 and design 0.5. The 13 evaluation questions are well specified and the limitations are stated honestly (one process model, a subset of BPMN constructs, two models). conclusions_supported is 1 because the claims stay modest and the two failure modes reported (executing a not-yet-enabled task; fabricating that an unperformed task was done) are directly evidenced. No artefacts.

entries.title: Enhancing declarative business process management availability through generative AI
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed Springer Process Science, with a Data Availability statement and a working repository at github.com/santos-wesley/Terpsichora. 2,000 generated MP-Declare models across 500 domains, two constrained-generation methods x two LLMs x two complexity batches, plus rediscovery from simulated event logs. baseline_or_control is 0.5: the comparison is within-study (Function Calling versus Structured Output) with no external ground truth or real-world model collection, which the authors identify as unavoidable given no MP-Declare benchmark exists. Limitations are candid about validation leaning on structural rather than semantic characteristics. Note for synthesis: this measures artefact quality, not any agent's compliance behaviour, so it carries no violation or completion data for RQ1.

entries.title: PolicyFaultBench: Mutation-Based Assurance of Policy Mediation and Proposal-Interface Conformance for Tool- Using AI Agents
entries.notes: Research Square preprint (University of Misan, 2 authors) - unreviewed, and the authors have no visible track record in the area, hence authority 0.5. Methodologically it is one of the more disciplined records here: a preregistered protocol (pfb-policy-generalization-v1), twelve first-order mutation operators applied to two independently implemented policy engines, always-allow / always-deny baselines, ablations, and 1,200 records replaying identically. objectivity and conclusions_supported are 1 because the paper reports its own preregistered 800/800 acceptance rule failing (791/800) and that mutation adequacy did not transfer to the external AgentDojo-derived corpus (2/12 kills). Construct validity is explicitly bounded - the prompt supplies the operation to transcribe - and the authors state no claims can be made about autonomous tool selection or planning. No artefact release found.

entries.title: Large Process Models: A Vision for Business Process Management in the Age of Generative AI
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed Springer KI - Künstliche Intelligenz, 15 authors spanning SAP Signavio and senior BPM academics (van der Aa, Polyvyanyy, Rinderle-Ma, Weber, Weidlich). Explicitly a vision/discussion paper: no benchmark, no baseline, no metrics, no artefacts. conclusions_supported is 1 and threats_discussed is 1 because it does not overclaim - it states outright that experimental evidence for LLM effectiveness in a process execution context is still missing, establishes feasibility only for Step 1, and declares that all non-academic authors work for a BPM software vendor. Valuable as framing and as evidence that the BPM community itself acknowledged the gap RQ1 targets, but it contributes no empirical result.

entries.title: Utilizing Large Language Models in Business Process Management: Applications and Challenges
entries.notes: Literature review in Journal of Computer Science (Cairo University, 3 authors); the venue is peer-reviewed, which is the only item scoring 1 besides aims. Design is a review of 42 studies selected from 86 screened with no reported search protocol, no inclusion criteria and no quality appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment, so design_appropriate is 0.5 and there is no baseline or metric of its own. conclusions_supported is 0.5 because performance figures in the text are relayed from reviewed papers rather than measured - notably a '72% usability improvement in a 17-company pilot' reported with no citation or method. Reported prior findings the authors merely cite are not this paper's own results. Challenges are discussed for the technology, not for the review's own methodology.

entries.title: Towards Modeling Human-Agentic Collaborative Workflows: A BPMN Extension
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed conference (Springer LNCS), University of Luxembourg / UOC / LIST, with a Sirius-based open-source editor at github.com/BESSER-PEARL/agentic-bpmn. The contribution is a BPMN metamodel extension (AgenticLane, AgenticTask, agentic gateways and message flows) validated only on a single running example modelled first in plain BPMN and then in the extension - a real but purely qualitative comparison, hence baseline_or_control 0.5 and design 0.5. metrics_defined is 0: no measure is defined and the authors state that a metric-based cognitive-effectiveness assessment against Moody's principles is future work. threats_discussed and conclusions_supported are 1 because the paper claims only expressiveness and states plainly that the extension has not yet been empirically evaluated. Directly relevant to RQ1's premise: it argues that relying on natural language for collaboration and reflection strategies produces ambiguity and misinterpretation.

entries.title: FRAMES: Guarded and Dual-Objective Skill Evolution for Agents in Policy-Governed Enterprise Workflows
entries.notes: Preprint from BMO Financial Group (7 authors) on a deployed financial document-auditing system. Directly contrasts B1 Raw LLM - the same policy supplied as natural-language instructions in the prompt - against the same agent bound to structured, step-ordered skill procedures derived from the same policy, on disjoint 210-case evolution and held-out test sets plus tau-bench, with paired McNemar (p = 0.0026) and bootstrap CIs, reported per risk category rather than as an aggregate. Section 7 Limitations is explicit about benchmark scarcity, dependence on feedback quality, the frozen base model, and evaluation cost capping the loop at a few hundred cases. data_or_artifacts_available is 0: FinDAS is internal production data and nothing is released. Garousi objectivity 0.5 for the vested interest in their own system, offset by category-level failure reporting.

entries.title: Enhancing Trust in LLM-Based AI Automation Agents: New Considerations and Future Challenges
entries.notes: Early IBM Research workshop position paper. No benchmark, no baseline and no quantitative result; the only assessment is a four-product yes/no/unknown comparison across trust dimensions, which is why metrics_defined is 0.5 and design 0.5. threats_discussed and objectivity score 1 because the authors state outright that the comparison is not detailed, may not reflect the tools' full abilities and reflects their own opinion after trying them, and they name the dimensions they excluded as too hard to assess. peer_reviewed_venue 0.5 for workshop-level review. Contributes a named catalogue of control considerations (prompt and output mediation, task/knowledge/application grounding, user feedback, pre-deployment dev-mode testing, safety guardrails, graceful failure) and the moderated-versus-autonomous action distinction, but no evidence.

entries.title: Real-Time Regulatory Intelligence Framework: LLM-powered compliance automation for financial services
entries.notes: Single author (Naga Krishna Mahesh Pulikonda) in World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences. Scores near the bottom of the corpus. There is no experimental protocol, no sample construction, no model identity, no statistical test and no released code or data, so design_appropriate is 0. The declared baselines - manual compliance review and rule-based systems - come with numbers, but those numbers are attributed inline to third-party references including vendor material, so they are reported prior findings rather than this paper's own results, giving baseline_or_control 0. The figures also contradict each other across sections: 94.2% overall interpretation accuracy versus 94.7% later; 97.3% versus 96.8% on prescriptive rules; 91.6% versus 84.7% on principle-based provisions; time-to-compliance 64.3 -> 7.8 days versus 63.7 -> 7.2 days; and 76.3% appears both as an assessment-time reduction and as a traditional-approach accuracy. Section 6 is a limitations-and-challenges discussion of deployment obstacles, not of study validity.

entries.title: Agentic AI for Regulatory Intelligence: Designing Scalable Compliance Lifecycle Systems in Multinational Tech Enterprises
entries.notes: Lowest-scoring record in the corpus. A narrative review in the International Journal of Scientific Research and Modern Technology proposing a multi-agent compliance lifecycle architecture. There is no experiment, no benchmark, no baseline, no metric and no artefact; the review states no search protocol, no inclusion criteria and no quality appraisal, so design_appropriate is 0. A full-text search finds five occurrences of 'limitation', every one of them describing limitations of traditional compliance models, RegTech or prior work - there is no discussion of this paper's own threats to validity, hence 0. conclusions_supported is 0 because the substantive claims are cited from others or openly speculative: the Amazon material is inferred from public sources and hedged as what its engines 'likely' do. The Governance-as-a-Service framing is a useful RQ2 idea, but nothing here is evidence.

entries.title: OpenMCPSpec: A Specification Framework for Robust, Governed, and Lifecycle-Managed Machine Communicable Processes in LLM-Agent Systems
entries.notes: Single author (Cognizant) at an IEEE conference (ICSCCC 2026), with schema, spec and test scripts released MIT at github.com/pvchaitu/mcp-agents-intents-schema-spec - which is why artefacts and venue score well while almost everything else does not. The entire evaluation is 20 tests (10 ACI, 10 CPR) against one SQLite MCP server with one model, and an independent two-sample t-test with p < 0.05 is claimed on that basis. metrics_defined is 0 because the reported metric contradicts its own definition: ACI is defined as the reduction in argument hallucination and gain in tool-calling accuracy, but the ACI table columns are execution times in seconds (1.996-3.110s baseline versus 1.591-2.598s). The declared zero-shot basic-MCP baseline with reported numbers earns 0.5. conclusions_supported is 0: the striking 9-of-10 policy-leak result is a binary pass/fail of the author's own enforcement layer against rules it was built to enforce, which is close to tautological, and the authors do not discuss the sample size as a limitation.
